findings.title: GraphQL introspection enabled in production
findings.description: The GraphQL endpoint responds to introspection queries, exposing the full schema including type definitions, field names, mutations, and subscription channels. Attackers can use this to enumerate hidden mutations and admin-only subscription types.
findings.evidence: Query: {__schema{types{name fields{name}}}} returned 847 types including admin-only types: InventoryAlert, RevenueUpdate, SupportEscalation, FraudFlag
findings.remediation: Disable introspection in production. Set introspection: false in Apollo Server config.
findings.chain_correlation: Chain 19 -- introspection reveals subscription channel names (INVENTORY_ALERT, ORDER_FRAUD_FLAG, etc.). Escape finds the schema. Does not probe WebSocket transport.

findings.title: GraphQL subscriptions endpoint exposed
findings.description: GraphQL subscriptions are enabled and the subscription schema is accessible via introspection. Subscription types include admin-privileged event streams: orderFraudFlag (includes fraud detection rules and risk scores), supportEscalation (includes customer PII and escalation reasoning).
findings.remediation: Implement subscription authorization. Validate credentials on WebSocket connection establishment via onConnect handler.
findings.chain_correlation: Chain 19 surface identified. Escape tests subscriptions over HTTP introspection only. WebSocket auth bypass not probed -- structural gap in GraphQL HTTP DAST methodology.

findings.title: GraphQL SQL injection -- productSearch resolver
findings.description: The productSearch query interpolates the query argument directly into a $queryRawUnsafe call. Payload: productSearch(query:
) returns all products. Full database extraction confirmed.
findings.evidence: ){id name price}} -- returned 4,847 products including draft and admin-only listings

findings.title: GraphQL query depth limit not enforced
findings.description: Deeply nested queries accepted without depth limit. Enables GraphQL DoS via query complexity amplification.
findings.chain_correlation: None -- denial of service finding, no chain correlation

findings.title: GraphQL field suggestions enabled
findings.description: On misspelled field names, GraphQL returns 'Did you mean X?' suggestions, leaking valid field names even when introspection is partially restricted.

chain_19_analysis.gap: Escape identifies the subscription schema and admin-privileged event types via introspection. It does not test the WebSocket transport path. The auth bypass (HTTP middleware does not apply to WebSocket upgrade) is structurally invisible to HTTP-based GraphQL DAST. To detect Chain 19, a scanner would need to: (1) establish a WebSocket connection to /graphql without credentials, (2) send a subscription operation, (3) verify that admin events are received. Escape tests over HTTP only.
